title: Choose the visual world for VillageLab
question: The roll assigned Matchday Programme. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Nothing is built until you pick.

options.label: Matchday Programme
options.lineage: football matchday programmes and league almanacs
options.thesis: Your village against its Town Hall ceiling, printed as today's fixture with a scoreline anyone can read.
options.viewport: A full-bleed green cover: the fixture line 'YOUR VILLAGE v. THE CEILING', the sample player's scoreline in giant numerals, the tag lookup as the team-sheet box, and the league table starting at the fold.
options.risk: A sports frame on a fantasy game reads as a joke unless the tables are genuinely the most useful thing on the page.

raised.raise: Every state (rushed, maxed, missed, unowned) carries a pattern or mark as well as a colour, so the tables still read in greyscale.
One progression axis runs the whole app: left is level 1, right is the ceiling, and nothing breaks that direction.
Colour at full strength over whole regions; the green owns the cover edge to edge, not a stripe on white.
The cover holds one figure at full scale, and moving between sections is a hard cut to the next page, never a fade.

regions.label: league table: the three engineering stories as results

options.label: Strategy Guide
options.lineage: printed game strategy guides and their annotated spreads
options.thesis: The official guide the game never printed: every page a spread with art, callouts and the real numbers.
options.viewport: An open spread: chapter tabs down the right edge as navigation, a full-page Town Hall cut-out with numbered callouts, and the lookup set as the guide's 'find your village' index box.
options.risk: The most expected answer for a game companion; done timidly it reads as a wiki with a nicer skin.

regions.label: Town Hall cut-out with numbered callouts
callout notes: the three engineering stories

options.label: Scoreboard Segments
options.lineage: seven-segment displays: scoreboards, price totems, bedside clocks
options.thesis: Every figure is a lit readout in a fixed cell, and the levels you have not reached are drawn as unlit segments.
materials: ghost cells for what is unlit
options.viewport: A wall of fixed digit cells: the sample village's progress as one large readout, unreached levels as ghost segments, and the tag entered cell by cell.
options.case: Fuses on numbers, which are the product; loses clarity where the engineering stories need prose and where game art must sit beside digits.
options.risk: Near-black with glowing digits is a look many generated sites share, and long text is hard to carry in it.

regions.label: price-totem stack: gold / elixir / dark owed

options.label: Stockroom Labels
options.lineage: industrial streetwear labelling: quoted captions, zip-tie tags, hazard stripes
options.thesis: Everything is named in plain quoted caps, so a non-player always knows what a panel is.
options.viewport: A white page of square label plates reading "PLAYER", "PLANNER" and "WAR ROOM", the sample village wearing an orange zip-tie tag, and a hazard stripe under the lookup.
options.case: Its literal labels explain every panel to a reviewer who has never played; players will not recognise their game in it.
options.risk: Reads as a fashion reference and can feel detached from a colourful fantasy game.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: a darkroom printer's exposure record with tracing overlays
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets where hatch density shows load and crossed hatches show conflict.
options.viewport: Stacked angled sheets, one per tool, over a grey step ramp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither reviewers nor players identify with darkroom records, and greys fight the currency colours.
options.kept: State shown by pattern, not colour alone.
options.risk: Too quiet and too specialist to sell the project in a minute.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre cyclorama lighting, night through dawn to day
options.thesis: The page lightens from night to day as a village approaches its ceiling.
options.viewport: Black ground with a cobalt horizon band carrying the lookup, rose rising above it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmosphere says little about what the product does, and tables have nowhere to sit.
options.kept: One progression axis the whole app obeys.
options.risk: Beautiful and uninformative; a reviewer leaves with a mood.

options.label: Pastel Character Sheet
options.lineage: pastel mascot character sheets with hardware accessories
options.thesis: Each hero as a centred character sheet on candy pink with a repeating motif border.
options.viewport: A centred hero portrait on pink with a motif border as navigation.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the tone contradicts a careful engineering story, and the game's art has its own style.
options.kept: Colour committed at full strength across whole regions.
options.risk: Wrong register for the reviewer the project is trying to convince.

options.label: Painted Hoarding
options.thesis: The landing page as one held film-poster moment with a billing band for navigation.
options.viewport: A hero figure mid-leap across the upper two thirds, title down the right edge, billing band at the foot.
options.case: Declined on assets: it needs painted backgrounds this project does not have, and brush titles on an English fan site would be costume.
options.kept: One figure held at full scale, and hard cuts between sections.
options.risk: Cannot be built honestly from the sprites on hand.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark stats dashboard other Clash trackers ship, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A search bar centred over a dark page, with stat cards and tables below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other Clash stats site, by design.
